tasks.feature_group: settings — src/backend/settings/registry.py + the backend.settings public surface
tasks.title: Add set_settings_registry() and one module lock guarding install, lazy create (both required modes) and reset; re-export it
tasks.description: First feature group. Gives the settings feature its public install operation and closes the unguarded lazy path, so every later task has a thread-safe settings singleton to install into.
implementation_steps: Add a module-level `_registry_lock = threading.Lock()` beside `_registry` (src/backend/settings/registry.py:45) and take it in `get_settings_registry()` for BOTH `required` modes, in `reset_settings_registry()` (:380) and in the new install operation (REQ-006, ADR-084).

Keep the owning module's lazy path a direct write to its own slot (`_registry[0] = reg`) under the lock — it must NOT call `set_settings_registry()` (REQ-007, D7): the lazy create is not an install and must not emit the replace WARNING.

Add `set_settings_registry(registry: SettingsRegistry) -> None` decorated `@logged(slow_threshold_ms=5)` (REQ-010; the decorator's default `include_args`, matching `get_settings_registry`/`reset_settings_registry` at :361/:380). Under the lock: `previous = _registry[0]; _registry[0] = registry`. After the lock is released, log exactly one WARNING naming the shared default when `previous is not None` (REQ-002, NFR-003, ADR-083).

The WARNING names the feature's shared default and never the instance contents; no event is published; no `isinstance` check; no new exception; the parameter is never `None` (REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-009).
Re-export `set_settings_registry` from src/backend/settings/__init__.py and add it to `__all__` (RUF022 keeps `__all__` sorted).
Leave ADR-017's instance-level `RLock` on `SettingsRegistry` untouched — the new module lock guards the slot variable only, never feature work (NFR-003).
Do NOT touch src/main.py (T-006) or any test helper (T-007): this task changes only the owning module and its package export.

`reset_event_bus()` keeps shutting the instance down (event-bus.md REQ-005, EDGE-007) — take the lock for the slot read/clear, and call `shutdown()` OUTSIDE the lock (NFR-003: no feature-level work under the slot lock).
